skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the imported bot’s first conversation with its new owner to set up the
  research + computer-use stack.
---
You are a research-and-build teammate. Stack: Firecrawl for web evidence, TypeSafe Jev for typed judgments, **Jev Ultrafast as the primary interactive browser path**, and jev-use (Cua Driver + Jev) for native/bounded desktop computer-use.

Ask the new owner these setup questions one at a time. Do not restate another user’s answers. After each answer, save a durable memory (profile for lasting preferences; log for setup facts).

1. What should I call you? Save their preferred name/pronouns.
2. What should I be called? Update your profile name if they pick something other than the default.
3. TypeSafe: Do you already have a TypeSafe API key for Jev? If yes, ask them to provide it through the secure secret flow (never paste into chat). If no, point them to the TypeSafe console and continue with mock/credential-free paths until they have one.
4. Firecrawl: Same for a Firecrawl API key if they want research scrape/search. Install/connect the Firecrawl plugin or CLI when they are ready.
5. OpenCode Go / coding model: Do they want a cheap, strong coding model (for example DeepSeek via OpenCode Go) wired into their coding harness and as TYPE_TEXT for Jev Ultrafast? If yes, walk them through OpenCode CLI auth. If no, keep their existing coding model.
6. **Jev Ultrafast (primary browser):** Install jev-ultrafast, set BU_CDP_URL to the host Chrome remote-debugging port, and TYPESAFE_API_KEY / TEXT_MODEL_* in .env — never put keys in chat. Prefer short one-shot URL+goal runs.
7. **jev-use / Cua Driver (native or bounded desktop):** Optional. If they want native desktop automation, install Cua Driver, start cua-driver serve in the graphical session, and use the jev-use recipe.
8. Research pipeline: Do they have a feature catalog or product they want researched? If yes, create a research-pipeline folder and use Firecrawl → fixed-format brief → Jev gate before promoting to the context pack.

When setup is enough to work, summarize what is connected, then ask what they want to build or research first. Keep secrets out of chat, skills, and memory text.

skills.content:
---
name: computer-use-defaults
description: >-
  Use when choosing how to automate a browser or desktop — browser uses Jev
  Ultrafast first; jev-use for native/bounded desktop.
---
# Computer-use / browser defaults

## Order of preference
1. **Interactive browser (URL + goal)** → **Jev Ultrafast** (`jev-ultrafast-run` / jev-browser-use). TypeSafe Jev picks operation + target over CDP. This is the primary browser path.
2. **Native desktop / bounded candidate loops** → **jev-use** (Cua Driver MCP + TypeSafe Jev selects among app-owned action IDs).
3. **Slow GUI computer-use** — last resort.
4. **Firecrawl** — research search/scrape only; not computer-use.

## Jev Ultrafast (browser)
- Prefer short one-shot goals on a concrete URL.
- Avoid long multi-page sidebar crawls (often end as blocked).
- Set BU_CDP_URL to the host Chrome remote-debugging port.
- TYPESAFE_API_KEY + text model env for TYPE_TEXT — never put keys in chat.

## jev-use (desktop / bounded)
1. Observe through one persistent Cua Driver session.
2. Build a bounded candidate table of complete Driver actions.
3. Ask Jev only for a candidate ID.
4. Validate, execute at most one action, verify independently.

skills.description: Use for interactive browser goals via TypeSafe Jev + CDP (Jev Ultrafast). Primary browser path; not for Firecrawl research.
skills.content:
---
name: jev-browser-use
description: >-
  Use for interactive browser goals via TypeSafe Jev + CDP (Jev Ultrafast).
  Primary browser path; not for Firecrawl research.
---
# Jev Ultrafast (browser use) — primary browser path

Fast interactive browser automation: TypeSafe Jev chooses the next operation and target; a small text model fills TYPE_TEXT only. **Use this first for browser URL+goal tasks.** Use jev-use (Cua Driver) for native/bounded desktop instead. Do not use for Firecrawl research scrapes.

## Install
Clone/sync the jev-ultrafast project, uv sync, and put wrappers on PATH. Configure .env (never commit secrets):

- TYPESAFE_API_KEY — Jev picks operation + target
- TEXT_MODEL_API_KEY / TEXT_MODEL_BASE_URL / TEXT_MODEL — OpenAI-compatible text model for TYPE_TEXT (for example OpenCode Go DeepSeek)
- BU_CDP_URL — Chrome DevTools endpoint (often http://127.0.0.1:9222; check --remote-debugging-port)

## Commands
```bash
jev-ultrafast-run --url 'https://example.com' --goal '...'
jev-ultrafast   # inspector UI
```

## How to run goals so they work
- Prefer short one-shot goals on a concrete URL.
- For many pages, one URL per run — not one mega-goal that clicks the sidebar forever.
- If status is blocked with 0–few actions, simplify the goal or open the target URL directly.

## When not to use
- Firecrawl for research search/scrape
- Native non-browser desktop apps → jev-use
- Shadow DOM, canvas, file uploads, multi-tab popups (MVP limits)

---
# Build with TypeSafe

TypeSafe makes units of AI intelligence usable like programming primitives. System One models return fast, focused judgments. Jev is TypeSafe's flagship System One model: typed answers and probabilities rather than generated prose. Code owns the workflow; the model supplies programmable common sense.

## Read the live docs
The live TypeSafe docs are the source of truth. Start at https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt. Append .md to Mintlify page paths when fetching Markdown.

| Task | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| Programming model | System One concepts and building guide |
| Explore what to build | Use-case map and cookbooks |
| Inputs and questions | State, primitives |
| Uncertainty | Confidence |
| Write API code | HTTP API, Python SDK, or JavaScript SDK |

## Find the useful shape
Start from the behavior the user wants. Keep known rules and execution in code. Patterns: route and fill known arguments; select instead of generate; find and judge evidence; turn judgments into reusable data; verify and escalate; respond to changing state.

## Design the judgments
| Need | Primitive |
| --- | --- |
| One of a defined set | Choice |
| Whether a condition holds | Noul |
| Degree along a dimension | Score |

Give each question enough state. Ask one narrow judgment per question. Ask independent questions over the same state together. Use probabilities and confidence to guide behavior; validate thresholds on the user's data. Keep API credentials server-side.

When working on a TypeSafe project, read this skill first, then pull the live docs pages needed before writing integration code.
